name: Ratsek Hut
near: Kashka-Suu — about 18 km as the crow flies (OSM marker); the Ala-Archa park's address on 2GIS is Kashka-Suu. The real starting point is the Ala-Archa alplager (mountaineering camp) (~12 km above the park checkpoint), from where it is 5.7–6 km on foot to the hut.
elev: About 3300–3400 m; sources disagree: 3240 m (kgnomad, 05.2026), 3300 m (travelbar.kg), 3360 m (asiamixtravel), ~3380 m (adventuresoflilnicki, 09.2026); in 2026 the Ministry of Emergencies wrote “about 3200 m”. Ascent from the alplager is ~1100–1350 m (asia-hikes: +1341 m).
short: Ratsek Hut is a legendary mountaineers' shelter on a moraine in the Ak-Sai gorge (Ala-Archa) at ~3300–3400 m, at the tongue of the Ak-Sai glacier; the most popular goal of a long day hike from Bishkek.
desc: Ratsek Hut stands on moraines in the side gorge of Ak-Sai in Ala-Archa Nature Park, at about 3300–3400 m, below the Ak-Sai glacier and the peaks Korona (4860 m), Svobodnaya Koreya (Free Korea) (4740 m) and Uchitel (Teacher) (4530 m). It is named after Vladimir Iosifovich Ratsek (1918–1980) — a Master of Sport, 1950 USSR high-altitude mountaineering champion and one of the pioneers of Kyrgyz mountaineering. At first a canvas tent stood here; the permanent shelter was built in 1969 and rebuilt by 2008. The hut is now run by Ak-Sai Travel: up to 35 beds in two shared rooms and a VIP room, a kitchen, a bathhouse/sauna, solar-panel electricity, open year-round. It is the base camp for climbs of Uchitel (1B) and other peaks of the Ak-Sai spur; for ordinary tourists it is the goal of a hard day hike past the Ak-Sai waterfall.
guide: Ratsek Hut is your first real “high-mountain” trophy near Bishkek: from the alplager it is about 6 km and +1300 m, usually 4–5 hours uphill. Set off from the alplager no later than 8 a.m. — the first electric bus from the checkpoint and an early start will save you from the afternoon thunderstorm. Landmarks along the way: the “Broken Heart” rock, the Tepshi plateau, the Ak-Sai waterfall (the last reliable stream before the steep scree climb) and finally the moraine with a view of the Ak-Sai glacier and Korona peak. If you are staying overnight, book a place with Ak-Sai Travel ($15 per bunk) and climb to the lake and the Uchitel glacier in the morning. The hut is named after the mountaineer Vladimir Ratsek — memorial plaques hang on the wall inside.
see: The Ak-Sai glacier and icefall from the moraine at the hut; the panorama of the peaks Korona (4860 m), Svobodnaya Koreya (Free Korea) (4740 m) and Uchitel (4530 m); the Ak-Sai waterfall on the way; a radial side trip (~4 km round trip) to the glacier and Lake Uchitel (asia-hikes); memorial plaques to mountaineers at the hut.
skip: You are not ready for ~1300 m of ascent in a day and steep scree on the last section — the Ak-Sai waterfall is enough for an easy walk. You don't tolerate altitude above 3300 m well: every season the Ministry of Emergencies evacuates tourists with altitude sickness from here. You arrive at Ala-Archa after lunch — you won't manage a round trip before dark.
diff: Moderate to hard for an unprepared tourist: 12–16 km round trip, ~1100–1350 m of ascent, maximum altitude ~3350 m (kgnomad: moderate, 14 km, +1500 m; asia-hikes: 6 km and +1341 m one way). The last section above the waterfall is steep scree and moraine. No technical skills are needed in summer; above the hut (glacier, peaks) is a mountaineering zone.
when: Late June to September: the trail has no deep snow and the weather is more stable (asiamixtravel); kgnomad says June to October. The hut is open year-round (Ak-Sai Travel), but in winter and spring the approach is avalanche-prone and requires winter gear.
hours: The hut receives guests year-round (Ak-Sai Travel); book via WhatsApp/e-mail on the site ak-sai.com. Ala-Archa park is open daily; electric buses run from the checkpoint to the alplager all day (hiking.kg says around the clock), bus No. 1 from Bishkek runs 08:00–19:00.
daytime: Start from the alplager before 8:00 (kgnomad) so you reach the top by noon: afternoons often bring clouds and thunderstorms, and you need to finish the scree descent in daylight (asiamixtravel). Morning has the best light on the glacier and Korona peak.
how: Bishkek → Ala-Archa park checkpoint: bus No. 1 from the old Usubaliev Square (50 som cash/40 som by card, 45–60 min) or a taxi. Since 01.05.2025 combustion-engine cars are left at the checkpoint; from there a free electric bus runs ~12 km to the alplager. From the alplager on foot up the Ak-Sai gorge: the “Broken Heart” rock → the Tepshi plateau → the Ak-Sai waterfall → a steep scree climb to the moraine and the hut (ilovekg). There is no road access to the hut.
needcar: Only as far as the park checkpoint (bus No. 1 or taxi); inside there is a free electric bus to the alplager, and beyond that only on foot. You don't need your own car.
self: Yes, in summer the trail is popular and easy to follow: bus No. 1 → electric bus → on foot. You need good physical shape, an offline map (there is no signal on the route) and an early start. Book an overnight stay in the hut in advance with Ak-Sai Travel. Going onto the glacier and peaks is only for experienced people or with a guide.
roadtype: Paved road to the checkpoint; inside the park, a paved road for electric buses to the alplager. Above that is a mountain trail; above the Ak-Sai waterfall it is a steep rocky climb and a moraine section with slippery scree.
traveltime: Bishkek → checkpoint: 45–60 min by bus No. 1; checkpoint → alplager: electric bus ~12 km. Alplager → hut: 5.7–6 km, 4–6 h up, 3–4 h down (ilovekg; asia-hikes: 4 h walking, 5–7 h with stops); the whole day takes 8–11 h.
stay: Ratsek Hut (Ak-Sai Travel, up to 35 beds): shared room $15/person, VIP $25/person, RedFox tent rental $15, your own tent — $3/person/day; heating $30 for 4 h, sauna $45/h, sleeping bag $10/night, kitchen rental $25/day (ak-sai.com, 2026). Nearby is the Light House hut in the Ratsek clearing (booking at the same place). Lower down are cottages and yurts at the Ala-Archa alplager.
net: There is no mobile network on the route or at the hut — download offline maps (asiamixtravel). The last reliable signal is around the checkpoint/alplager (group 6 data, operator not confirmed). The hut has solar-panel electricity (Ak-Sai Travel).
entry: Entry to Ala-Archa Nature Park from 11.06.2026: adults 250 som, children 7–14 years 180 som, under 7 free (24.kg; group 6 data). There is no separate fee for the climb to the hut; overnight stay and camping are paid to Ak-Sai Travel ($15 bunk, $3 own tent). The old figures (80 som per person, 500 som per bunk — asia-hikes) are out of date.
transfer: Bus No. 1 — 50 som cash/40 som by card (2025–2026); the electric bus inside the park is free; taxi Bishkek → checkpoint ~$12–18 one way, private transfer $40–90 (kgnomad, 2026); the travelbar.kg group hike — 350 som per person including transport.
bring: Trekking boots with stiff soles and poles (slippery scree), a waterproof shell, fleece, hat and gloves (at the hut it is +10–12 °C by day and frost is possible at night — kgnomad), 1.5–2 L of water (the last stream is at the waterfall), a snack, category 3–4 sunglasses and SPF cream, a headlamp, cash for the entry fee. For an overnight stay — a sleeping bag (or rent one for $10).
warn: Altitude 3300+ m: risk of altitude sickness — on 29.06.2026 the Ministry of Emergencies evacuated a tourist from the route, and there were similar cases in 2024–2025 (24.kg). Don't gain altitude too fast, drink water, and if you have symptoms, descend and call 112. The scree above the waterfall is slippery and there is rockfall under the slopes; get back before dark. There is no signal. Outside summer it is avalanche-prone. Since 01.05.2025 combustion-engine cars are banned from entering the park — electric bus only.
food: At the hut you can order food from Ak-Sai Travel: breakfast $12, lunch $20, dinner $15, single dishes/sandwiches $10 (ak-sai.com, 2026); there is a kitchen for self-catering. Lower down there is a cafe and restaurant at the Ala-Archa alplager. The sources name no local specialties at the hut itself.
reviews: Google Maps: 4.7/5, 230 ratings (as of 03.10.2026). TripAdvisor: the “Ratsek Cabin” page (d10235109) with reviews; AllTrails: the route “Ala-Archa — Ak-Sai Racek Hut and Glacier” — 224 reviews (07.10.2026). Pros: views of the glacier and Korona peak, the atmosphere of a mountaineers' shelter, closeness to Bishkek. Cons: heavy, steep scree at the end, crowded on summer weekends, the altitude makes itself felt.
p.sum: There is no road to Ratsek Hut — only a 6–9 km trail with +1100–1350 m from the Ala-Archa alplager. The easiest way: bus No. 1 or a taxi to the park checkpoint (entry 250 som), a free electric bus to the alplager and 3–6 hours on foot past the Ak-Sai waterfall. Set off before 8:00 and preferably spend the night in the hut: a bunk with Ak-Sai Travel is $15, dinner $15. In summer (July–August) the trail has no snow and needs no technical gear. From mid-October to mid-April you need crampons on the approach, and above the hut, on the glacier and the peaks, you can't manage without experience or a guide.
p.apps.0.title: From Bishkek via the Ala-Archa checkpoint, electric bus and the Ak-Sai gorge trail (the only one)
p.apps.0.from: Bishkek (≈40 km to the park checkpoint)
p.apps.0.route: Bishkek → Ala-Archa Nature Park checkpoint (bus No. 1 / taxi) → free electric bus ~12 km to the Ala-Archa alplager (~2100 m) → on foot up the Ak-Sai gorge: the “Broken Heart” rock → the Tepshi plateau → the Ak-Sai waterfall → steep scree and moraine → Ratsek Hut (~3300–3400 m)
p.apps.0.km: Bishkek — checkpoint ≈40 km; checkpoint — alplager ≈12 km; alplager — hut 5.7–6 km (ilovekg, asia-hikes), about 9 km according to Nomad's Land
p.apps.0.time: Bishkek — checkpoint 45–60 min; ascent 3–6 h, descent 3–4 h; whole day 8–11 h
p.apps.0.surface: Paved road to the checkpoint and a road for electric buses to the alplager. Beyond that is a mountain trail: past the Ak-Sai waterfall a steep rocky climb and slippery moraine
p.apps.0.vehicle: on foot (combustion-engine cars are left at the checkpoint since 01.05.2025)
p.apps.0.season: Without gear — late June to September; from mid-October to mid-April crampons are needed on the approach to the hut (summitx). The hut is open year-round
p.apps.0.last: Fuel stations, ATMs and supermarkets — in the southern districts of Bishkek and on the road to Ala-Archa. The last cafe and reliable signal are at the checkpoint and the alplager. On the trail there are no shops and no network
p.apps.0.parking.d: Parking at the park checkpoint (~700 spaces, per group 6 data). You can't go further by car, only by electric bus
p.apps.0.parking.price: The parking price at the checkpoint is not confirmed; entry 250 som per person (since 11.06.2026)
p.apps.0.trail.d: Ala-Archa alplager (the electric bus terminus): the trail goes up the left side into the Ak-Sai gorge
p.apps.0.haz: Altitude sickness at 3300+ m: the Ministry of Emergencies evacuated tourists in 2024–2026 (24.kg, 29.06.2026). Scree and rockfall above the waterfall, afternoon thunderstorms. Blizzards are possible until about 20 June (summitx), avalanche danger from October to April
p.transport.0.from: Old Usubaliev Square, Bishkek → Ala-Archa checkpoint
p.transport.1.details: Ordering from the city is no problem; for the way back it is better to book a car in advance at the checkpoint
p.transport.2.details: Every 10–15 min during the day; since 19.02.2026 a Doppelmayr gondola also operates in parallel (600/400 som, closed on Tuesdays)
p.transport.3.details: 5.7–9 km and +1100–1350 m; there are no horses or porters on the trail
p.transport.4.details: Run + hike to Ratsek Hut and Lake Uchitel: minivan and guide
p.transport.6.details: 2 days: day 1 — ascent and a night at Ratsek Hut, day 2 — climb of Uchitel peak (4530 m, +1030 m) and descent. Transport, guide, accommodation, sleeping bag, lunch and dinner and park entry are included; personal gear is not included
p.transport.7.details: Alpine school “7-Day Mountaineering Course” based at Ratsek Hut: rock, rope, ice, climbs of Ratsek peak (2A) and Uchitel. IFMGA guides. Transport, meals, accommodation and group gear are included; personal technical gear is not. Also the Uchitel + Yukhin program (11 days) — $1500/person.

p.onsite.horses.0.notes: The sources offer no horse or pack services to the hut; porters in Kyrgyzstan can be hired through travel companies for about $50/day (Journal of Nomads)
p.onsite.other.0.details: Ak-Sai Travel runs mountaineering and ice-climbing courses based at the hut. In winter people ice-climb on the frozen Ak-Sai waterfall; the safe season for ice routes is from mid-October to early May
p.onsite.other.2.details: No separate rules for Ala-Archa park were found; it is a specially protected natural area, so it is better to clear a flight at the checkpoint
p.onsite.camping: You can pitch tents around the hut: your own tent — $3/person per day, RedFox tent rental — $15 (Ak-Sai Travel, 2026). Water comes from the stream at the waterfall and meltwater at the hut. It is worth boiling or filtering it
p.onsite.photo_spots: The moraine at the hut with a view of the Ak-Sai icefall and Korona peak (morning light), the Ak-Sai waterfall on the way, the Tepshi plateau with a panorama of the Ala-Archa valley

p.rent.1.price: prices are on rentik.kg, not found in open sources
p.rent.3.where: Hut/Ak-Sai Travel: per Explore-Share, “some technical gear can be rented on site if available” — check in advance. To buy: Red Fox, Alex.kg, Gerger Sport in Bishkek
p.rent.3.price: rental prices for crampons and ice axes not found
p.svc.toilets: At the checkpoint and the alplager; there is a toilet at the hut. No toilets on the trail
p.svc.water: The stream at the Ak-Sai waterfall is the last reliable source on the climb; at the hut it is meltwater (boil it). A thermos of boiling water at the hut — $5
p.svc.shop: No shops in the park; buy food in Bishkek
p.svc.atm: Bishkek; none in the park. At the hut they accept dollars or som, check the payment method
p.svc.fuel: Fuel stations in the southern part of Bishkek / on the road to Ala-Archa
p.svc.mobile: There is a network at the checkpoint and the alplager; none on the trail or at the hut
p.svc.medical: The nearest hospitals are in Bishkek
p.svc.rescue: Ministry of Emergencies — 112; rescuers regularly evacuate tourists with altitude sickness from the route to the hut (24.kg, 2025–2026)
p.iti.0.title: One day from Bishkek
p.iti.0.plan: 6:30 taxi or the first bus No. 1 → 7:30 checkpoint (entry 250 som) → electric bus → 8:00 start from the alplager → 9:30 Tepshi plateau → 11:00 Ak-Sai waterfall → 12:00–12:30 the hut: lunch ($10–20) and the moraine → 13:30 descent → 16:30–17:00 alplager → electric bus → evening in Bishkek. Only for the well prepared
p.iti.1.title: 2 days with an overnight stay
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: start from the alplager after lunch, climb to the hut, dinner and the night (bunk $15, dinner $15). Day 2: sunrise on the moraine, a radial trip to the glacier and Lake Uchitel (2–3 h), descent, evening in Bishkek. Option for mountaineers: day 2 — climb of Uchitel peak (1B) with a guide
p.iti.2.title: What to combine
p.iti.2.plan: The Ak-Sai glacier is right at the hut, so it is one trip. Ala-Archa National Park: the Ak-Sai waterfall, the Adygene gorge, the gondola — for the next day. The Chunkurchak gorge — 40–60 min by car via Kashka-Suu, the following day
p.season: January–February: stable and sunny, −10…−20 °C at the hut, approach only for experienced people, with crampons. March–April: unstable, windy, avalanche danger. May: the first half is sunny, from the second half snowfalls. June: blizzards are possible at the hut until about the 20th. July–August: no snow, up to +25 °C by day, the hut is crowded, rockfall danger grows. September–early October: “golden autumn”, stable, little wind, getting colder down to −10 °C. Late October–November: snowfalls. From mid-October to mid-April you need crampons on the approach (summitx)
p.budget.economy: ≈1000–2500 som per day: bus No. 1 round trip 80–100 som, entry 250 som, electric bus 0, a snack from Bishkek 300–500 som, lunch at the hut $10–20 if you wish. With an overnight stay — plus a bunk $15, dinner and breakfast $27 (≈4000–5000 som in total); a weekend group tour — 1300 som (Ulush Travel, 2025) or 350 som (Travelbar)
p.budget.comfort: ≈$150–650 per person: taxi or transfer $40–90, entry, 2 days at the hut with meals ≈$70, a guide $80–100/day (Journal of Nomads); a ready-made 2-day tour with a climb of Uchitel ≈CA$611
p.permits: No border-zone permit is needed. Only an Ala-Archa park ticket is required at the checkpoint: 250 som, children 7–14 years — 180 som, under 7 — free (since 11.06.2026). For climbs, foreigners may need a climbing permit (Ak-Sai lists a “climbing permit” separately in the exclusions) — check with the operator
p.access: With small children, older people, or with a stroller — no: a steep climb of 1100+ m and scree. With teenagers — only if they are in good shape. With a stroller only the area around the alplager is accessible. Dogs: no special rules for the park were found, but a dog is inconvenient on scree and in the hut
p.gaps.0: rental prices for crampons and ice axes in Bishkek and at the hut
p.gaps.2: daily rate of a local mountaineering guide for Uchitel (only a rough guide of $80–100/day)
